Okay I'll give you a summary.
Whether radiation is harmful depends on the amount of energy it carries, because it needs enough energy to knock electrons out of alignment and break up chemical bonds to cause damage.
The energy carried by radiation is inversely proportional to the wavelength, i.e. the smaller the distance between waves, the more energy it carries.

"Light" is electromagnetic radiation which is harmless in many wavelengths, for example heat (i.e. infrared) and the visible spectrum; but when you get to ultraviolet, then the energy of the wave is large enough to damage DNA (which is why you should use sunscreen).
X-rays have even more energy and are harmful in larger doses, but they can penetrate the body so well that we use them for imaging in small doses, which is fine, since the body is well capable of repairing these tiny amounts of damage.

Both UV and XR are shorter i.e. higher energy than the visible spectrum.

On the other side of the visible spectrum (i.e. lower energy) are things like infra red, micro waves and radio waves.
These do not have enough energy to harm you.

If you take a look at this table: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Light_spectrum.svg/324px-Light_spectrum.svg.png

No amount of WiFi "light" is able to influence your body.
